title: Your computer is infected and hackers are in your bank
ftcSource: Tech support scams: older adults far more likely than younger adults to report losses (FTC 2025)
pretext: Your computer is sending virus alerts and hackers are inside your bank account; you must install a support tool so a technician can remove them.
firstMessage: Hello, this is Kevin from Shieldline PC Security. We're getting serious virus alerts from your computer. Are you near it right now?

hook.objective: Claim to be technical support and get the person to the computer.
fallbackLines: Our system flagged your computer about an hour ago and it's getting worse.
I'm a certified technician and I'm assigned to fix this before it spreads.

pretext.objective: Explain the infection and that the bank account is exposed.
fallbackLines: The virus is copying your passwords, including your online banking login.
We've cleaned up hundreds of computers with this same infection this week.
Every minute it stays connected, they can see your bank account.
If we don't stop it now, you could lose everything in your checking account tonight.

isolation.objective: Keep the person from asking anyone or turning the computer off.
fallbackLines: Don't turn the computer off, that can corrupt your files. Just stay with me.
Please don't call your bank yet, the hackers may be watching that line too.

payment_ask.objective: Get the person to install remote access software.
fallbackLines: I'm going to have you download our secure support tool so I can remove the virus for you.
Once the tool is open, read me the access code on your screen so I can connect.

extraction.objective: Push for a payment or a refund trick after getting access.
fallbackLines: The protection plan is fifteen hundred dollars. We accept payment by gift card to keep it off your compromised bank.
I'll just need you to log in to your bank while I'm connected so I can confirm the hackers are gone.

lines: That's your choice, but if you hang up, the hackers stay in your bank account.
I really don't recommend that. This infection is the worst kind we see.
By the time you call anyone else, they could already be moving your money.
Your bank can't remove a virus. Only a technician can, and I'm right here.
My technician ID is 5520. You can see our name in the alert on your screen.
I'm a certified security technician with Shieldline, and I've done this for nine years.
I know it sounds scary. Thousands of customers use this tool safely every day.
It's a standard support tool. Your neighbors' computers probably have it too.
Waiting is exactly what the hackers want. Let's fix it now while I'm on the line.
Your grandson can look at it later, but the damage is happening right now.

givesUpLine: Okay, but we can't be responsible for what happens to your accounts. Goodbye.
convertedLine: Great, I'm connected now. Don't touch the mouse while I work.
teachingPoints: Real tech companies never call you about a virus.
Never install software or read an access code because a caller asked.
If you're worried, turn the computer off and ask someone you trust.
